title: Kinetic Slush in Dissipative Rydberg Arrays
authors: Hufeng Wen, Ya-Xin Xiang, Qun-Li Lei, Thomas Pohl, Zhengyang Bai, Yu-Qiang Ma
abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of a kinetic slush state realized via facilitated excitations in a two-dimensional dissipative Rydberg atom array. Utilizing kinetic Monte Carlo simulations in the strong dephasing regime, we show that tuning the laser detuning to compensate for nearest-neighbor interactions enables facilitated dynamics, while residual next-nearest-neighbor interactions induce kinetic frustration. This competition gives rise to an emergent slush phase characterized by pronounced dynamical heterogeneity and the coexistence of liquid- and solid-like configurations. By probing its nonequilibrium real-time evolution, we uncover a dynamical crossover from isotropic spreading to one-dimensional constrained growth, which can be continuously tuned by the frustration strength. Within this crossover regime, the slush dynamics generate fractal cluster geometries and generalized Ornstein-Zernike spatial correlations. Finite-size scaling analysis supports the system's proximity to criticality. Our findings establish driven-dissipative Rydberg systems as a highly controllable platform for engineering complex nonequilibrium soft-matter phenomena.
summary: This paper explores the complex, non-equilibrium dynamics of a 'kinetic slush' phase in a 2D array of dissipative Rydberg atoms. By tuning the laser detuning and introducing kinetic frustration via next-nearest-neighbor interactions, the system exhibits a rich crossover between different growth regimes. The findings establish these driven-dissipative quantum systems as a powerful tool for engineering complex soft-matter phenomena.
main_problem: The study investigates the nonequilibrium dynamics of a kinetic slush state realized in a two-dimensional dissipative Rydberg atom array.
main_result: The system exhibits a slush phase characterized by dynamical heterogeneity and a crossover from isotropic spreading to one-dimensional constrained growth, tunable by kinetic frustration.
method: Kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulations are employed to analyze the time evolution of the system's density and spatial correlations.
model_or_system: The system is a 2D dissipative Rydberg atom array governed by a Hamiltonian including van der Waals interactions, evolving under a Lindblad master equation in the strong dephasing regime.
key_observables: Mean Rydberg density $ho(	au)$, local activity $K_j$, generalized Ornstein-Zernike spatial correlations, and fractal dimension $d_f$.
important_parameters: Laser detuning ($\Delta$), kinetic frustration strength ($\eta$), and the ratio of NNN coupling to dissipation ($\eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the strong dephasing limit ($\gamma \gg \Omega$) and often truncates interactions to nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor terms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model setup, steady-state spatial configurations, local activity heatmaps, and the time evolution of the mean Rydberg density $ho(	au)$ for varying frustration strengths.
paper_structure: The paper develops the model Hamiltonian and master equation, analyzes the dynamics in different frustration regimes ($\eta=0$, finite $\eta$, $\eta 	o \infty$), and quantifies the resulting spatial structures using correlation functions and fractal analysis.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable platform (Rydberg arrays) to model complex, non-equilibrium soft-matter physics, bridging concepts from frustrated magnetism and driven-dissipative quantum dynamics.
